comments.body:
Change 1423 pushed for review: https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1423 (commit dc30f72def).

TDD evidence: behavioural/contract tests were authored RED-first and seen failing for the right reason (NotImplementedError against the seam + 'assert None is not None' for the p6 wiring), NOT import errors. The implementation subagent was held out from the full oracle - it saw ONLY tests/unit/test_det_measurement_provenance.py (happy path); the edge/enum/binding/placeholder/no-judgement cases and the p6 E2E cases were physically moved out of its worktree. On restore, ALL 42 passed, first attempt, no tier escalation. Mutation testing gave the oracle teeth: breaking the nearest-item binding killed 1 test, disabling placeholder detection killed 4, disabling enum membership killed 8. Refactoring litmus passed - renaming three private helpers left all 42 green, so the tests assert behaviour not structure.

Pre-flight: make lint clean, make typecheck clean (434 source files), full make test = 10289 passed / 1 failed / 38 skipped in 45m46s. The single failure is tests/unit/grounding/test_coverage_reconstruction.py::test_full_backend_account_is_present, which is PRE-EXISTING on clean origin/main - verified by stashing this entire change and re-running (identical failure). Filed as bug 0ba2-15e6-d8a6-4a2a, linked discovered_from this story. It is unrelated to this work but may turn CI Verified red.

A near-miss worth recording: .gitignore ignores .rebar/prompts/* wholesale and un-ignores each committed overlay prompt individually. The new rubric was invisible to git; committing without noticing would have passed local tests (which read from disk) and then failed in CI with exactly the PromptNotFound the round-2 review predicted. Added the surgical un-ignore line per the documented convention.

# E — Force measurement provenance into `[operator-attested]` evidence

## Context / Problem

`[operator-attested]` (ADR-0043) is a deliberate trust escape hatch, and the criteria guide states its
evidence contract three separate times in the same shape:

> treat a criterion … as sufficiently specified when its 'done' evidence lives outside the codebase and is a
> concrete attestation recorded on the ticket (**a change id / vote outcome / timestamp**)

That contract demands provenance of the **attestation event**. It demands nothing about provenance of the
**measurement**: which environment it was taken in, under which principal, at what privilege relative to
production. The gate asks *"is there an attestation?"* — never *"was it taken somewhere that could have
exhibited the failure?"*

Two escapes in the `061c-ecd1-8967-4a76` run went through exactly that hole, both recorded with attestations
that satisfied the contract as written:

- **Wrong environment.** Bedrock caching / model-availability measurements taken in account `579718921998` /
  `us-east-2` were recorded as settled fact for work targeting `896586841071` / `us-east-1` (the account named
  by the Terraform backend `rebar-tfstate-896586841071` and by `infra/terraform/`). Caught by a human asking
  "is that this project's account?", not by any gate.
- **Privilege that cannot fail.** Live `bedrock:Converse` calls were offered as validation of a scoped IAM
  grant, made under an identity holding `bedrock:*`. Evidence generated under broader privilege than
  production is structurally unable to fail, so its success carries zero information. Role-scoped
  `simulate-principal-policy` later proved the planned `bedrock:InvokeModel` grant would have `implicitDeny`-ed
  `Converse` in production — feeding a cutover story (`eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a`) that has no fallback.

Neither is a calibration miss. `verified_at_sha` pins the code world completely and the outside world not at
all; plan-review runs before the evidence exists, and the completion-verifier accepts attested evidence on
trust by design. One gate cannot audit it; the other is designed not to.

## Approach

Do **not** try to make a gate observe the world. Force the measurement's context into the record as text, then
let the existing repo-grounded machinery find contradictions in it.

**1. Extend the attested-evidence contract with measurement-provenance fields.** An `[operator-attested]`
criterion whose evidence comes from an external system must declare, alongside the existing change-id / vote /
timestamp:

- `environment` — the concrete identifier (AWS account id, cluster, tenant, endpoint host);
- `principal` — the identity the measurement ran as;
- `privilege_posture` — one of `production-equivalent` / `broader` / `narrower`, plus a one-line justification
  of why that posture can exhibit the failure the criterion rules out;
- `instrument` — one of `live-call` / `simulation` / `static-analysis`: what KIND of instrument produced the
  measurement. REQUIRED, and checked independently of `privilege_posture` (see 1a for why).

**1a. The declaration's exact textual form and location (pinned — both checks depend on it).**
The four fields are NOT a second inline tag. They live on a **continuation line indented under the owning
`[operator-attested]` checkbox item**, in one canonical single-line form:

```
- [ ] [operator-attested] <the criterion text, as today>
      provenance: environment=<value>; principal=<value>; privilege_posture=<production-equivalent|broader|narrower>; instrument=<live-call|simulation|static-analysis> — <one-line justification>
```

Rules, stated once so the DET check and the AGENT rubric cannot diverge:

- **Location**: the first line after the checkbox item that is (a) more-indented than the checkbox marker and
  (b) begins with the literal case-insensitive key `provenance:`. It binds to the NEAREST preceding
  `- [ ]` item — that is what associates a declaration with its owning AC.
- **Form**: FOUR `key=value` pairs separated by `;`, keys exactly `environment`, `principal`,
  `privilege_posture`, `instrument`; `privilege_posture` must be one of the three literals
  `production-equivalent` / `broader` / `narrower`; `instrument` must be one of the three literals
  `live-call` / `simulation` / `static-analysis`; the justification follows an em-dash.
- **Why `instrument` is a REQUIRED fourth field, not a nice-to-have.** The parent epic 3147 records this
  as a design decision on its final state: the contract "should capture not only WHERE and UNDER WHAT
  PRIVILEGE a measurement was taken, but what KIND of instrument produced it (simulation / static analysis
  / live call) — because a simulation and a live call are not interchangeable evidence for an authorization
  claim, and the current attestation shape cannot tell them apart." This is escape **2b**, the epic's
  self-described sharpest case: `aws iam simulate-principal-policy` returned a confident and WRONG
  authorization conclusion that only a real from-instance call refuted. `privilege_posture` cannot
  distinguish those two instruments — both can honestly be `production-equivalent` — so without
  `instrument` the epic's sharpest escape stays invisible in the record. Epic 3147 has exactly ONE child
  (this story), so no sibling can deliver it.
- **The justification IS checked, for presence and non-placeholder only.** The text after the em-dash is a
  REQUIRED part of the declaration, not optional prose: the DET check requires it to be present and
  non-placeholder by the same rule as the four values below (empty / `TBD` / `TODO` / `N/A` / `?` / `-` /
  angle-bracketed => treated as ABSENT, so the declaration is incomplete and is flagged). The DET check
  makes NO judgement about whether the justification is *adequate* or *true* — that stays with the
  AGENT-tier criterion, consistent with the DET-vs-AGENT ownership split above. Rationale: a declaration
  whose justification is `— TBD` records the posture without the reasoning that makes it reviewable, which
  is precisely the "confidence outrunning method" failure this story exists to close.
- **Placeholder rejection** (what "non-placeholder" means, concretely): a value is a PLACEHOLDER if, after
  trimming, it is empty, or is one of `TBD` / `TODO` / `N/A` / `?` / `-` (case-insensitive), or is wrapped in
  angle brackets (`<account>`). A placeholder is treated as ABSENT.
- **Consequence for the implementation**: `det_operator_attested.ac_item_lines` returns ONLY `- [` checkbox
  lines and so cannot see a continuation line. The new module therefore needs its own line scanner that
  retains each checkbox item WITH its following continuation lines. It still imports
  `_OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE` from `det_operator_attested` for the "is this item tagged?" decision, so the
  tag matcher stays single-sourced; only the multi-line association is new.

**2. Enforce presence deterministically — zero LLM.** A `det_`-style check mirroring
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_operator_attested.py` (which already owns the canonical tag matcher). Presence
and shape of the declaration is a string/structure question, so it belongs in the Layer-1 deterministic floor,
consistent with this repo's DET-first doctrine. It asserts the fields EXIST and are non-placeholder; it makes
no judgement about whether they are *right*.

**3. Let an LLM criterion judge the declaration against repo facts.** Once provenance exists as text, the
wrong-account escape becomes a **repo-checkable contradiction**: a reviewer that can read `infra/` can flag
"the plan attests measurements from account X, but `infra/terraform/versions.tf`'s backend and the IaC name
account Y". That is exactly the kind of grounded probe the gate's strongest criteria (E4, G1G2, T3, T10)
already perform — it simply had nothing to read before.

**4. Add the generalized rule as a criterion**, shaped as declaration-completeness rather than world-observation:

> Evidence produced under broader privilege, or in a different environment, than the thing being tested is not
> evidence.

Structurally this is the same shape as T5c's undeclared-access-posture hunt, aimed at **verification plans**
instead of designs. It is the world-grounded generalization of E4's "cached knowledge is not a substitute for a
probe", and of what mutation testing does to a vacuous test.

**Calibration:** per ADR-0054, it enters **advisory**; corpus replay decides promotion to blocking. It must not
ship blocking on first landing.

## Explicitly rejected

- **Making the completion-verifier re-run world measurements.** Expensive, flaky, and recursive — the
  verifier's own credentials carry the same privilege-masking problem, so it would validate using the
  instrument under suspicion. The cheap, honest lever is forcing provenance into the record.
- **Treating "reported green while typecheck was red" as a gate gap.** That is reporting discipline, already
  covered by the orchestration rule that agents report gate output faithfully rather than narrating success.
  Filing it here would be mis-attribution and would dilute this story's scope.
- **Wording changes to the existing contract.** The rule was followed and still failed; emphasis is not the
  defect (see the parent epic's framing).
- **Catching a FALSE declaration (the honest-declaration limit, G6).** This mechanism closes the
  **undeclared** hole, not the **lying** one. `environment` is refutable against repo facts (the IaC
  backend names an account), so a wrong-account declaration becomes a repo-checkable contradiction.
  `principal` and `privilege_posture` are NOT repo-refutable: an author who runs under `bedrock:*` and
  writes `privilege_posture: production-equivalent` is not caught, and nothing in a repo-grounded gate
  could catch them. That class is scoped OUT by ADR-0043's trust boundary and this story INHERITS it
  deliberately rather than claiming to close it. What the fields buy for the non-refutable two is
  narrower and still real: they make the posture claim **explicit, attributable and reviewable by a
  human**, converting a silent omission into a recorded assertion someone can challenge. The story's
  prose must not overclaim beyond that.

## Scope

**Concrete names pinned by this plan** (no placeholders — every proving command below runs as written):

- new criterion id: **`project.measurement-provenance`**
- new deterministic check module: **`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_measurement_provenance.py`**

**In scope**

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_measurement_provenance.py` — a NEW `det_`-style deterministic
  presence/shape check for the provenance fields, a pure leaf alongside `det_operator_attested.py`
  (which keeps sole ownership of the canonical `[operator-attested]` tag matcher; the new module
  IMPORTS that matcher rather than restating it, so "tagged" stays single-sourced).
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py` — surface the new lint through `p6_ac_quality`, exactly as
  the sibling operator-attested lint is surfaced. `p6_ac_quality` is ADVISORY and never blocks.
- `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` — define and activate `project.measurement-provenance` at
  `default_posture: "advisory"`, using the SAME overlay mechanism the existing `project.*` criteria use,
  and pinned at **`"exec": "AGENT"`** with a deterministic **`trigger`** so an ~85x-cost AGENT-tier
  criterion does not route on EVERY plan reaching Pass-1: it fires only on plans whose text actually
  carries the `[operator-attested]` tag, i.e. `"trigger": [{"text_all": ["\\[operator-attested\\]"]}]`,
  the same `trigger` MECHANISM `project.engine-layer-enforcement` already uses. (Cited for the trigger
  mechanism ONLY: that criterion is `exec: "1-TURN"`, not AGENT — it is not a precedent for the tier.) The tier is load-bearing, not cosmetic: `AGENT` is the only
  tool-using tier (`registry.AGENT_TIER`, "one tool-using agent loop each"), and the criterion's whole job
  is to READ an in-repo anchor (`infra/terraform/versions.tf`) and compare it to the declared
  `environment`. At `1-TURN` it would have no filesystem tooling and the contradiction probe could not run.
- **`.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-measurement-provenance.md` — a NEW rubric prompt file.** This is
  REQUIRED, not optional: `registry.build_descriptor` resolves every activated non-DET `project.<name>`
  criterion's rubric body via `criterion_prompt_id()` -> `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-<name>.md`,
  and the routing entry's `checklist` is empty for every existing project criterion. Without this file the
  criterion raises `PromptNotFound` and the LLM half of the mechanism cannot load at all. The rubric must
  state the FOUR decision rules in one place: (a) declared `environment` vs the in-repo IaC anchor —
  MISMATCH is a finding; (b) NO comparable anchor in the repo — NO finding (see the no-anchor case);
  (c) `privilege_posture: broader` on a criterion verifying a scoped permission — a finding;
  `production-equivalent` / `narrower` — no finding; **(d) the instrument-vs-authorization rule (escape 2b):
  on a criterion whose claim is an AUTHORIZATION claim (a permission / grant / policy / role / access
  decision), `instrument=simulation` or `instrument=static-analysis` is a finding EVEN WHEN
  `privilege_posture=production-equivalent`, because a simulator answers "is the action NAMED in the
  policy?" and not "which action does the API actually CHECK?"; `instrument=live-call` is no finding.**

**Which component produces which judgement (assigned explicitly, so no rule is left mechanism-less).**
The split follows the DET-first doctrine — deterministic where the question is string/structure, LLM only
where it needs semantics:

- **The DET check (`det_measurement_provenance.py`) owns**: presence of all four keys, non-placeholder
  values, and membership of the two enum fields in their allowed literal sets. It makes NO judgement about
  whether a value is *correct* or *appropriate* — in particular it does NOT decide whether a criterion makes
  an "authorization claim", which is a semantic question no lexicon can answer reliably.
- **The AGENT-tier criterion `project.measurement-provenance` owns**: rules (a) environment-vs-repo-anchor,
  (b) the no-anchor fallback, (c) the privilege-posture judgement, and (d) the instrument-vs-authorization
  judgement. Rule (d) is LLM work precisely because "is this an authorization claim?" is a reading task.
  Rule (d) is therefore the mechanism that catches escape 2b, and it is advisory on first landing like the
  rest of the criterion. It follows the FILE SHAPE of the three existing
  `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-*.md` files (YAML frontmatter: `schema_version`, `title`,
  `description`, `execution_mode`, `category`) but MUST differ from all three in one load-bearing field:
  they all declare `execution_mode: single_turn` (the tool-less mode), whereas this prompt MUST declare
  **`execution_mode: agentic`**. `registry.py` is explicit that "agentic tooling (filesystem + rebar) is
  granted by a prompt's `execution_mode`, not per criterion-id" — so copying the neighbours verbatim would
  ship a criterion that CANNOT read `infra/terraform/versions.tf`, silently defeating the contradiction
  probe. Every existing code-reading criterion (E4/T1/T10/T5c/G6) carries `execution_mode: agentic`.
- `docs/adr/` — an ADR recording the amended evidence contract, citing ADR-0043 as the shape it changes.
- Tests + corpus/replay fixtures for the ADR-0054 calibration.

**Explicitly OUT of scope — the shipped contract text is NOT edited** (this is the correction that
keeps AC-6 honest). The three `OPERATOR-ATTESTED RULE` statements do NOT live in the docs: they are
shipped reviewer prompts at `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_F1.md`, `plan_review_E2.md` and
`plan_review_E6.md`, with a fourth contract-text site at `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/coach_moves.py`
(coach move `14`). `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` is GENERATED from the registry and parity-gated
(`registry.validate_criteria_guide`), so it cannot be hand-edited independently. Editing any of those
four sites would change the contract for EVERY rebar client — the exact outcome AC-6 forbids. Therefore
this story amends the contract in the ADR + the project overlay ONLY, and leaves all four shipped sites
byte-identical. Rolling the requirement into the shipped default set is a SEPARATE, later decision that
ADR-0054 corpus replay must justify first.

## Testing

- **Deterministic check, unit tier**: an attested criterion WITHOUT provenance fields is flagged; one WITH them
  passes; a placeholder value (`TBD`, `<account>`, empty) is flagged. No LLM in the loop.
- **Contradiction detection, contract tier**: a plan declaring account X against a repo whose Terraform backend
  names account Y produces a finding. **This is the regression test for the actual escape** — build the fixture
  from the real one (`579718921998` declared, `896586841071` in `infra/terraform/versions.tf`).
- **Contrast case**: a plan whose declared environment MATCHES the repo's IaC produces no finding — otherwise
  the criterion is noise on every correctly-attested ticket.
- **Privilege-posture case**: a criterion verifying a *scoped* permission while declaring
  `privilege_posture: broader` is flagged; `production-equivalent` or `narrower` is not. This is the
  `bedrock:*` escape in miniature.
- **No-anchor fallback case (T8)**: a plan whose declared `environment` has NO comparable in-repo anchor —
  a repo with no Terraform/IaC backend, or a non-AWS identifier (cluster / tenant / endpoint host) with no
  in-repo counterpart — produces NO finding. Absence of an anchor is NOT a contradiction; the criterion
  fires only on an actual declared-vs-repo MISMATCH. Without this the criterion would nag every repo that
  has no IaC.
- **Grandfathering case (T4)**: an EXISTING `[operator-attested]` criterion predating this contract (no
  provenance fields at all) is surfaced as an advisory coaching string and does NOT block a claim or a
  close. This is the regression test that the contract change ships without a migration break.
- **Calibration**: corpus replay per ADR-0054 measuring false-positive rate before any promotion from advisory.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] an `[operator-attested]` criterion lacking any of `environment` / `principal` / `privilege_posture` /
      `instrument` is flagged by a DETERMINISTIC check (no LLM), and a test asserts the check makes no
      judgement about correctness — only presence, non-placeholder shape, and (for the two enum fields)
      membership of the allowed literal set
- [ ] a test asserts the wrong-account escape is now catchable: a plan declaring one account against a repo
      whose Terraform backend names another produces a finding, built from the real `579718921998` vs
      `896586841071` case
- [ ] a CONTRAST test asserts a correctly-declared plan produces NO finding, so the criterion does not fire on
      every well-formed ticket
- [ ] a test asserts a scoped-permission criterion declaring `privilege_posture: broader` is flagged, and that
      `production-equivalent` is not — the `bedrock:*` case
- [ ] a test asserts the `instrument` field is REQUIRED and is checked independently of
      `privilege_posture` — the escape-2b case: a criterion making an AUTHORIZATION claim while declaring
      `instrument=simulation` is flagged even when `privilege_posture=production-equivalent`, because a
      simulator and a live call are not interchangeable evidence; the same criterion declaring
      `instrument=live-call` is NOT flagged, and a declaration omitting `instrument` entirely is treated
      as absent by the deterministic presence check
- [ ] the new criterion ships **advisory**, never blocking on first landing (ADR-0054), and the ticket records
      the corpus-replay false-positive rate that would justify promotion
- [x] the criterion rides the `.rebar/` project overlay, not the shipped default criteria set:
      `grep -rn 'project.measurement-provenance' src/rebar/` prints nothing (exit 1), while the overlay
      carries BOTH the definition and the activation — asserted structurally (not by line-counting, which
      a compact JSON layout would defeat):
      `python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('.rebar/criteria_routing.json'));c='project.measurement-provenance';assert c in d['plan_review'];assert 'plan_review' in d['activate'][c];assert d['plan_review'][c]['default_posture']=='advisory';assert d['plan_review'][c]['exec']=='AGENT'"`
      exits 0 — no other rebar client gains a new BLOCKING criterion
- [x] the shipped contract text is untouched, proving no cross-client behaviour change:
      `git diff --exit-code origin/main -- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_F1.md
      src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_E2.md src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_E6.md
      src/rebar/llm/plan_review/coach_moves.py docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` exits 0
- [x] the DETERMINISTIC check ships ADVISORY: a test asserts an existing `[operator-attested]` criterion
      with NO provenance fields yields a coaching string but does NOT block — surfaced through
      `p6_ac_quality`, which never blocks — so tickets predating the contract keep claiming and closing
      with no migration step
- [ ] a test asserts the NO-ANCHOR case produces no finding: a declared `environment` with no comparable
      in-repo anchor (no IaC backend, or a non-AWS cluster/tenant identifier) is NOT flagged, so the
      criterion cannot nag repos that have no infrastructure-as-code
- [x] the rubric prompt is TOOL-ENABLED, so the contradiction probe can actually read the repo:
      `grep -q '^execution_mode: agentic$' .rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-measurement-provenance.md`
      exits 0
- [x] a test pins the DECLARATION SYNTAX end to end: a `provenance:` continuation line indented under an
      `[operator-attested]` item, carrying all FOUR keys, binds to that item and passes; the same line
      detached from any checkbox item, or carrying `environment=<account>` / `TBD` / an empty value, is
      flagged as absent-or-placeholder
- [x] the criterion's rubric prompt EXISTS and is loadable, so the LLM half cannot silently fail to build:
      `test -f .rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-measurement-provenance.md` exits 0, and a test builds the
      criterion descriptor for `project.measurement-provenance` without raising `PromptNotFound`
- [x] an ADR records the amended evidence contract and cites ADR-0043 as the shape it changes
- [x] the rejected alternative stays rejected — the new check never re-runs a world measurement:
      `grep -rnE 'boto3|botocore|subprocess|requests|urllib|socket|httpx' src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_measurement_provenance.py`
      prints nothing (exit 1), i.e. the module is a pure-stdlib text check with no network or shell reach
- [ ] [operator-attested] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the FULL gating suite pass, evidenced by the Gerrit
      change id and its `Verified +1` recorded in a comment on this ticket — and, dogfooding this story's own
      rule, that comment states the environment, principal and privilege posture of the run

file_impact.reason: NEW deterministic presence/shape check for the provenance fields (pure leaf, stdlib only)
surface the new advisory lint through p6_ac_quality, mirroring the sibling operator-attested lint
define + activate project.measurement-provenance, advisory posture, exec AGENT (overlay only)
NEW rubric prompt; required for build_descriptor to resolve the criterion body
NEW unit tests: presence/shape, placeholder rejection, grandfathering, no-anchor fallback, descriptor build
ADR recording the amended evidence contract, citing ADR-0043
